analyst.summary: Ambuja Cements has become the flagship of Adani's cement roll-up -- absorbing Sanghi, Penna, and soon ACC and Orient into a single ~110+ MTPA platform, debt-free and funding its own expansion. FY26 volumes were a record 73.7 million tonnes, but a large chunk of the reported profit jump was one-off tax credits rather than real operating improvement -- strip those out and normalised profit actually fell year-on-year in the March quarter, and the stock's true earnings multiple is closer to 40x than the ~22x headline number suggests. Returns on capital have also come down sharply (to ~5.6%) as the company issued a lot of new shares to fund its acquisitions. The company's own cost targets for the coming year assume real improvement that hasn't shown up yet, and the broader cement industry is bracing for margin pressure as a wave of new capacity comes online nationally. We rate this a Hold: a well-capitalised, well-run consolidation story, but not cheap, and not without real execution risk over the next few years.
